HEY, I’M

JoshJunarto

Student. Singapore.

I’m at ASRJC. I teach myself code, tinker with Linux, and take a camera out when I need a change of view.

01 / A LITTLE BACKSTORY

Before ASR,
Maris Stella.

I was in the media club’s EXCO. Cameras, lights, microphones — and a team behind the scenes making things happen.

02 / A LITTLE CLOSER

A small room.
A lot going on.

Code, cameras and a few unfinished questions. I like keeping things minimal and working on engineering projects.

03 / A DIFFERENT WAY TO LOOK

Lights. Camera.
Action.

Everyday details. The city at night. Photography gives me another reason to go outside and look closer.

04 / HOW I LEARN

I learn by
taking it apart.

AI, networks, operating systems: I want to see the moving parts. PyJosh is one small attempt, built with Python and JAX.

05 / MY CORNER

My desktop
has opinions.

I use Linux. I care about how it looks — and what it costs in memory. The tiny details matter to me.

06 / THINGS I’M FIGURING OUT

Some questions
become projects.

A homework tracker. A neural-network framework. A different approach to an algorithm. All opensource on GitHub.

07 / ALONG THE WAY

A few
achievements.

AI Fundamentals
IBM
Python Essentials
Cisco

08 / OTHER PERSPECTIVES

Better with
other people.

Media club taught me coordination. Being a class leader is teaching me to listen, stay open to suggestions, and help where I can.

09 / WHAT COMES NEXT

Still a student.
Still exploring.

AI, silicon, energy. A lot to learn, and plenty of room to change my mind.
